# Whether every member of a ball is positive, one-limb center

Kernel `ball_positive_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $0 < x$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty, $X$ the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \ne \emptyset \text{ and } 0 < x \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c$ and radius $r$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $0 < x$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty: the answer is exact.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius compared with the center (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_positive_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_positive_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# Whether every member of a ball with a one-limb center is positive, and the ball is not empty
# (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", the row of certainly_positive()): c - r > 0, decided
# exactly as r < c. False for the empty set (a NaN compares false) and for the whole line (+inf < 0
# is false). The comparison of Ball<T, 1>::certainly_positive, written by hand in
# include/kairn/ball.hpp. Exact.

m = lt(r, c)
```
